A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same ECBench/ECEval study and contain the complete main paper and supplementary Sections 6-10. Their text, tables, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, blind GPT-4o and human results on ECBench in Tables 2-5, alongside original dataset analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and dataset analyses, including model and human performance in Tables 2-5.

M1.justification: Benchmark construction, question filtering and ECEval's combined binary and multilevel scoring remain unchanged. The revised explanation in Section 4.5 introduces no procedural change; supplementary scoring prompts are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScanNet, MultiScan, HM3D and self-collected videos, covering static scenes, dynamic scenes and hallucination questions across the same 30 capabilities.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2-5, including GeLM, AlanaVLM, the general LVLMs, blind GPT-4o and humans. Figure 5 retains the same comparison of ECEval, binary scoring and multilevel scoring.

E3.justification: The 386-video, 4,324-question evaluation, model configurations, input frame counts, uniform frame sampling and scoring procedures are unchanged. Appendix 9 retains the same temperature and experimental prompts.

E4.justification: The frame-count comparisons, ECEval examples in Figure 5, supplementary question illustrations and dataset analyses are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Reporting remains based on the same point estimates, without added confidence intervals, significance tests or evaluation seed/run summaries. Existing repetition information for question screening is also unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and rankings in Tables 2-5 and the results displayed in figures are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains GPT-4o-[32f] at 50.35 overall and humans at 94.96; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs or derivations. The capability definitions, robot assumptions and evaluation definitions remain unchanged, including their supplementary descriptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: ECBench's 30-capability benchmark, ECEval and the identified weaknesses of current LVLMs. The conclusion is reflowed onto page 8 without changing its substance.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 replaces continued difficulty understanding scene dynamics with the more categorical statement that Video-LVLMs 'fundamentally' lack this ability. Section 4.2 also removes 'in simple scenes' from the inferred navigation/manipulation usefulness. These locally strengthen interpretation; Appendix 10's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data availability statement and supplementary implementation information are unchanged, including temperature 0.2, API/model-serving details and classification, inference and grading prompts.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 narrows its characterization of GeLM from mainly 'trained and evaluated' on XR-device videos to mainly 'trained' on them. This is a limited change to a prior-work description; the same 42 references, related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain.

P1.justification: v2 shortens several passages in Sections 4.1-4.5, revises affiliation and corresponding-author information, and adds a funding acknowledgment. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Page numbers are removed, selected discussion sentences gain bold emphasis, and text reflow brings the entire conclusion onto page 8. Figures, table structures and captions are retained; appendix page content is visually identical apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: The methods, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and appendices remain unchanged. Local prose edits improve concision but slightly weaken qualifications in Sections 4.1-4.2; the stronger dynamic-scene wording also overlaps with an already categorical statement in Section 4.3. These limited editorial and interpretive changes leave the paper's overall scientific support and usefulness essentially unchanged.
